description:
Project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)

Goal
- Deliver a vetted, versioned “tuning profiles pack” for Redwood’s current and near-future GPU fleet (H100, B200, L40S) that selects the best-known runtime configuration per hardware SKU and workload shape.
- Document expected behavior and trade-offs (latency/throughput/memory) so SRE, Infra, and customer-facing teams can reason about performance changes and safely roll out.

Scope
- Runtime tuning knobs (kernel selection/variants, scheduler/batching heuristics, KV cache and memory allocator settings, prefill/decode prioritization, concurrency limits).
- Host-level and container-level recommendations where Redwood controls them (CPU pinning, NUMA placement guidance, hugepages, CUDA env vars), with clear separation of “required” vs “best-effort” depending on deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- A reproducible benchmarking protocol and acceptance thresholds per SKU, integrated into perf-canary / benchmark-lab.
- Observability additions required to validate “expected behavior” (e.g., per-stage latency breakdown, queueing time, kernel fallback counters, OOM/fragmentation signals).

Non-goals
- Inventing new kernel implementations from scratch for every model family (focus is packaging, selection, and safe defaults; kernel work is incremental and targeted).
- Customer-specific bespoke configs (but the pack should allow controlled overrides with guardrails).

Key stakeholders / teams
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor), Hiro Tanaka (kernel team), Sofia Ivanova (scheduling), Noah Patel (runtime architecture), Grace Kim / Yuki Sato / Omar El‑Sayed / Lena Fischer / Marcus Reed (implementation + perf).
- Applied ML / perf: Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois, Arjun Desai (benchmark methodology + quantization interactions).
- Infra & SRE: Neha Kapoor, Irene Choi, Vanessa Ortiz (fleet constraints), Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (safe rollout + incident readiness), Allison Grant (metrics/dashboards).
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien (release trains, changelog discipline).
- Product/Dedicated: Lauren Bishop (customer-facing performance expectations and Dedicated SLO implications).

Deliverables
- A runtime-visible “profile pack” artifact (config schema + per-SKU defaults + versioning + compatibility rules).
- Confluence docs: profile reference, expected behavior, rollout/runbook, benchmarking protocol, and an ADR capturing design decisions.
- CI/perf gating: profile correctness + regression detection on representative workloads; canary rollout playbook.

Phases / timeline (illustrative, Q1–Q2 2026)
1) Discovery + requirements (2 weeks): collect fleet constraints, top workload shapes, baseline performance.
2) Profile schema + selection logic (2–3 weeks): encode profiles, implement selection and override rules, add instrumentation.
3) Benchmark + validation (3–4 weeks): run benchmark matrix on H100/L40S and early B200 nodes; tune thresholds.
4) Rollout + documentation (2–3 weeks): staged canary in Hosted, opt-in for Dedicated, guidance for Private; publish “expected behavior” and troubleshooting.

Constraints / risks
- Avoid tail-latency regressions under mixed workloads; ensure profile changes are observable and reversible.
- Fleet heterogeneity (driver/CUDA versions, PCIe vs SXM, MIG/no-MIG) must be surfaced in compatibility checks.
- Profiles must be safe defaults: explicit guardrails for memory headroom, fragmentation, and preemption/queueing.

How it fits Redwood
- Supports Redwood’s differentiation on predictable serving economics by making performance behavior repeatable across hardware generations and deployment modes, and by enabling transparent, documented performance profiles for internal and customer-facing use.

files.description: High-level overview: what the tuning profiles pack is, who owns it, supported SKUs (H100/B200/L40S), and how selection/overrides work across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Config schema definition (fields, validation, precedence) and deterministic selection rules by GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, model family, and workload shape.
Expected behavior on H100: latency/throughput characteristics by workload bucket, memory headroom assumptions, known trade-offs, and common failure modes.
Expected behavior on L40S: constraints vs H100, recommended batch/concurrency defaults, and stability guidance (OOM/fragmentation prevention).
B200 early-access expectations: provisional profile defaults, compatibility notes, and what metrics must be watched during bring-up.
Benchmark plan: workload buckets, prompt/response length distributions, model set, metrics captured, and pass/fail thresholds per SKU.
Step-by-step validation playbook: run commands, dashboards to check, regression triage flow, and how to file follow-up issues.
ADR capturing key decisions: why a versioned profile pack, where selection lives (runtime vs control plane), override guardrails, and rollback strategy.
Infra constraints doc: which instance types map to H100/B200/L40S, driver/CUDA baselines, MIG policy, and capacity caveats that impact tuning.
SLO guardrails for rollout: which latency percentiles and error rates block rollout, required dashboards, and canary escalation criteria.
Dashboard + alert spec: metrics needed to compare profiles (queueing, kernel fallbacks, KV cache hit rates, fragmentation, OOM), tags/labels, and alert thresholds.
Internal release note draft announcing the profile pack, default behavior changes, rollout status, and upgrade notes.
Epic/umbrella issue: Hardware tuning profiles pack (project setup, milestones, links to docs/PRs, and cross-team stakeholders).
Implement profile schema + validation (JSON/YAML), including compatibility checks (SKU/driver/CUDA) and safe default constraints.
Runtime selection logic: choose profile at startup and per-model load; define override precedence (fleet defaults vs customer pin).
Scheduler tuning: workload buckets + queue policy adjustments for tail latency under mixed prompt lengths.
Kernel tuning: H100 attention kernel variant selection + fallback rules; define counters/telemetry for kernel choice.
Memory/KV cache tuning: compaction thresholds, allocator knobs, and fragmentation signals; define expected failure behavior.
L40S profile definition and constraints; produce initial defaults and run baseline benchmarks.
B200 bring-up checklist (early fleet): compatibility gate, benchmark matrix subset, and rollback plan.
Integrate benchmark matrix into benchmark-lab CI; publish artifacts and store results with profile version tags.
Perf canary gating: detect regressions when profile defaults change; define automatic bisect inputs (profile version, kernel set).
Observability additions: add runtime tags for profile_id, sku, and scheduling mode; export counters/histograms.
Docs: Confluence expected behavior pages for H100/L40S/B200 and troubleshooting guide; review with SRE/Infra.
Rollout plan: staged enablement in Hosted, Dedicated opt-in, and Private deployment guidance; define success criteria.
Release engineering checklist: versioning, changelog entries, LTS branch strategy, and backport policy for profile fixes.
Investigate CPU/NUMA pinning recommendations impact (host-level tuning) and document when it applies.
Dedicated/Private overrides: allow per-customer profile pin with guardrails; ensure auditability and safe rollback.
PM spec: customer-facing expectations for Dedicated performance consistency; what to surface (or not) in customer docs and SLAs.
Design task: Console/ops UX for showing active hardware profile and profile version in debugging views (minimal UI spec).
Scratchpad capturing candidate knobs, hypotheses, and owner assignments; links to initial benchmark results and PRs.
Early draft of the profile pack config format (examples for H100/L40S) including comments and open questions.
Spreadsheet-style table: benchmark matrix (models, prompt/response sizes, concurrency), raw metrics, and computed deltas vs baseline.
Benchmark results for H100 runs (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory), with notes about anomalies and reruns.
Benchmark results for L40S runs and stability notes (OOM thresholds, fragmentation behavior, acceptable concurrency caps).
Early B200 smoke test results (limited matrix) and bring-up issues (driver/CUDA mismatches, kernel fallback rates).
SRE working checklist for rollout: dashboards, alarms, canary cohorts, rollback steps, and on-call comms template.
Infra memo: expected B200 fleet timeline, driver/CUDA standardization plan, and what variance must be handled by profiles.
Mapping of new metrics/tags needed to validate profile behavior; notes about cardinality limits and aggregation strategy.
Release plan draft: dates, required sign-offs, documentation checklist, and backout plan if perf regressions appear.
PM draft for how to explain tuning profiles to Dedicated customers (what improves, what might change, how to pin/rollback).
Retro notes after initial launch: what went well, what broke (if anything), and follow-ups for v1.1.
Add profile pack config loader + schema validation; initial H100/L40S profile definitions behind feature flag.
Runtime: profile selection logic by GPU SKU + driver version; include override precedence and logging.
Scheduler: introduce workload buckets and adjust queue prioritization for mixed prefill/decode; includes benchmarks and guardrails.
KV cache: tune compaction thresholds per profile; add counters for compaction time and fragmentation estimates.
Kernel selection: add H100 attention kernel variant ‘v3’ and fallback rules; export kernel_choice metric.
L40S: cap default concurrency and adjust preemption/backpressure defaults; add notes in config examples.
B200: add provisional SKU detection + compatibility gate (refuse unsafe defaults, require explicit profile version).
Observability: tag latency histograms with profile_id and sku; add new metric for scheduler_queue_ms.
Runtime config: add ‘profile_version’ pin and allow customer override with guardrails; includes audit log hook.
Fix: prevent profile mismatch when model reloads across GPU pools; regression test added.
Docs in-repo: add config examples and comments for profile fields; update runtime config reference.
Feature flag rollout: enable profile pack for small Hosted canary cohort; add kill-switch and safe rollback path.
Hotfix: revert overly aggressive batching default that increased p99 latency on a mixed workload; includes incident references.
Add profile-aware admission control: prevent overload by adjusting queue limits based on SKU and memory headroom.
Integrate profile pack version into /health and debug endpoints for faster on-call triage.
Refactor: isolate per-SKU defaults into a dedicated module; reduce config drift and add unit tests.
Add benchmark matrix runner for H100/L40S; persist results with profile_version and git sha tags.
B200 smoke suite: minimal workloads + sanity thresholds; mark as allowed-to-fail initially with tracking issue.
Add canary checks comparing latency deltas when default profile changes; integrate with Slack notifications.
New dashboards: ‘Runtime Profiles’ overview (profile_id adoption, p95 by profile, kernel fallback counters).
Expose profile pack config + override values via Helm chart values for Private installs; document defaults.
Private installer: detect GPU SKU and warn if running unsupported driver/CUDA combos for selected profile version.
Internal/external docs draft: ‘Performance profiles by hardware’ page; includes expected behavior tables and caveats.
CI: add profile schema validation step and golden config snapshots; block merges on invalid profile definitions.
Add runtime log summarizing active profile, key knob values, and detected hardware at startup for debugging.
Improve scheduler instrumentation: separate queueing vs compute time in traces; validate against expected behavior doc.
Follow-up: adjust L40S KV cache headroom settings to reduce OOM risk; update thresholds and tests.
Thread coordinating kickoff: owners for kernel/scheduler/benchmarks/docs; links to ENG epic and initial doc drafts.
Discussion about profile schema fields and override precedence; debate about where selection logic should live.
ADR review thread: concerns about config drift, version pinning, and rollback; requests for explicit guardrails.
Kernel team thread: H100 attention kernel variant comparison; sharing microbenchmark snippets and perf deltas.
Scheduler tuning thread: mixed workload buckets; quick back-and-forth on queue limits and p99 regression risk.
KV cache compaction tuning: what counters to add; agreement on ‘expected behavior’ signals for fragmentation.
Infra notes on fleet heterogeneity (driver/CUDA spread) and implications for profile compatibility checks.
SRE thread: defining rollout SLO gates and which alerts should page vs ticket; request for kill-switch semantics.
Dashboards planning: metric names, tag cardinality concerns, and initial mockups for ‘profile adoption’ panels.
Release coordination: which PRs must land for runtime-1.22, doc deadlines, and backport policy discussion.
Thread about L40S stability: OOM thresholds observed, proposed headroom settings, and next benchmark reruns.
B200 bring-up: early node quirks, driver mismatch errors, and agreement to add a hard compatibility gate.
Perf-canary integration thread: what should block merges vs warn; linking to perf-canary PR and Linear tasks.
Root-cause discussion for a small p99 regression during canary; deciding whether to adjust batching default.
Incident coordination thread for elevated tail latency after profile tweak; handoff between on-call and runtime owners.
Thread collecting post-incident follow-ups: add metrics, tighten gates, update expected behavior docs.
Rollout checklist iteration: defining canary cohorts (region/model mix) and rollback trigger thresholds.
Fleet ops thread: mapping instance types to SKUs and how to expose SKU metadata cleanly to runtime.
Docs coordination: where Confluence pages should live, review assignments, and which tables must be included.
Thread on override guardrails: preventing unsafe pins (e.g., low headroom settings) and how to audit overrides.
Alert tuning: kernel fallback rate alert thresholds and when it indicates a real performance issue vs expected behavior.
Benchmark-lab rerun coordination: seed selection, run ordering, and handling noisy results across regions.
Thread reviewing profile pack versioning strategy: semantic-ish versions, migration notes, and compatibility matrix.
Go/no-go thread for enabling profile pack defaults in Hosted; sign-offs from SRE/Infra and last-minute concerns.
Post-launch monitoring: early adoption metrics, customer workload spot-checks, and list of minor follow-ups.
Thread on adding debug endpoint fields for active profile; discussion of security implications and visibility.
On-call feedback: what signals were missing during regression triage; proposed runbook updates.
Kernel microbenchmark thread: edge case with long context windows; deciding whether to change kernel fallback conditions.
Infra confirmation: standardizing driver/CUDA baseline for B200; timeline and interim exceptions.
Thread about making Dedicated opt-in for profile changes; discussion with Product on customer expectations.
Product + runtime thread: how to message performance profile changes to Dedicated customers and what to expose in Console.
Console/ops UX thread: minimal UI changes to show profile_id and profile_version; tie-in to DES task.
Thread tracking documentation status: reviewers pinged, open TODOs for expected behavior tables and troubleshooting.
Backport discussion: which profile fixes must go into LTS branch; risk assessment and QA coverage.
Thread finalizing rollback automation: who can trigger, what gets reverted (profile version vs knobs), and audit trail.
Thread about follow-up v1.1 ideas: refine workload buckets, add more hardware variants, tighten perf thresholds.
Customer ticket: reports higher p99 latency after a runtime upgrade; includes environment (Dedicated H100) and links to canary investigation.
Customer ticket: intermittent OOM on L40S pool under burst traffic; triage notes point to profile headroom settings and workaround.
Internal helpdesk: request to add ‘active profile’ to standard on-call debug bundle; includes approvals and implementation link.
Customer ticket: asks how to pin a known-good profile version during a POC; support shares guidance and opens follow-up doc task.
Technical deep dive transcript with an enterprise prospect on H100 vs L40S performance expectations; action items to share benchmark methodology and Dedicated rollout options.
Dedicated performance sync transcript: customer questions about variability across regions and how profile versioning affects SLOs.
CS-led call transcript following a latency escalation; aligns on mitigation (pin profile), timeline for fix, and monitoring plan.
Company CRM record for an enterprise prospect evaluating Dedicated H100; notes include performance requirements, need for profile pinning, and linked technical deep dive.
Company CRM record for a mid-market customer using L40S pool; notes include OOM concerns, agreed workaround, and linked SUP ticket.
Company CRM record for a regulated customer exploring Private; notes include need for deterministic performance guidance and documented ‘expected behavior’ per SKU.
Email thread: Mateo aligns Runtime/Infra/SRE on scope, owners, and target release train; includes links to ENG epic and early Confluence outline.
Release thread: go/no-go checklist for runtime-1.22 including profile pack gating, documentation readiness, and rollback plan.
Infra leadership thread: decision on standard driver/CUDA baseline for B200 fleet and exceptions handling; requests compatibility gates in runtime.
Product thread: draft messaging to Dedicated customers about profile versioning/pinning, expected behavior, and how to request changes safely.
